location_zh: 第 17 章《加拉帕戈斯群岛》
text_en: The archipelago is a little world within itself, or rather a satellite attached to America, whence it has derived a few stray colonists, and has received the general character of its indigenous productions. Considering the small size of the islands, we feel the more astonished at the number of their aboriginal beings, and at their confined range. Seeing every height crowned with its crater, and the boundaries of most of the lava-streams still distinct, we are led to believe that within a period geologically recent the unbroken ocean was here spread out. Hence, both in space and time, we seem to be brought somewhat near to that great fact--that mystery of mysteries--the first appearance of new beings on this earth.
text_zh: 这片群岛本身就是一个小世界，或者说是依附于美洲的一颗卫星，从那里得到了几个零星的移民，也承袭了本土生物的总体特征。想到这些岛这么小，它们的本土生物数量之多、分布范围之窄，就更叫人吃惊。看到每一座高地顶上都是火山口，大多数熔岩流的边界还清清楚楚，我们不由得相信，在地质上很近的年代，这里还是一片完整的大洋。因此，无论在空间上还是时间上，我们似乎都被带到了那个伟大的事实——那个谜中之谜——的近旁：地球上新生物最初的出现。

location_zh: 第 17 章《加拉帕戈斯群岛》
text_en: I have not as yet noticed by far the most remarkable feature in the natural history of this archipelago; it is, that the different islands to a considerable extent are inhabited by a different set of beings. My attention was first called to this fact by the Vice-Governor, Mr. Lawson, declaring that the tortoises differed from the different islands, and that he could with certainty tell from which island any one was brought.
text_zh: 我还没有提到这片群岛自然史中远为最引人注目的特点：不同的岛屿在相当程度上住着不同的一批生物。最先让我注意到这一点的是副总督劳森先生，他说各个岛上的象龟各不相同，任何一只龟拿来，他都能确定是从哪个岛上来的。

text_en: And though it may seem very strange to talk of post-offices in this barren region, yet post-offices are occasionally to be found there. They consist of a stake and a bottle. The letters being not only sealed, but corked. They are generally deposited by captains of Nantucketers for the benefit of passing fishermen, and contain statements as to what luck they had in whaling or tortoise-hunting. Frequently, however, long months and months, whole years glide by and no applicant appears. The stake rots and falls, presenting no very exhilarating object.
text_zh: 在这片荒凉的地方谈论邮局，似乎非常奇怪，可这里有时确实能找到邮局。它们就是一根木桩加一只瓶子，信不仅封了口，还塞上了瓶塞。这些邮局一般是南塔克特来的船长们为路过的渔人留下的，信里说的是他们捕鲸或捕龟的收成如何。然而常常是一个月又一个月、一年又一年过去，都没有人来取。木桩烂了、倒了，那景象叫人一点也提不起精神。

location: Sketch First, The Isles at Large
text_en: Take five-and-twenty heaps of cinders dumped here and there in an outside city lot; imagine some of them magnified into mountains, and the vacant lot the sea; and you will have a fit idea of the general aspect of the Encantadas, or Enchanted Isles. A group rather of extinct volcanoes than of isles; looking much as the world at large might, after a penal conflagration.
text_zh: 拿二十五堆煤渣，随手倒在城外一块空地上；想象其中几堆放大成山，那块空地变成大海——你就对魔法群岛的总体面貌有了个恰当的印象。与其说它是一群岛，不如说是一群死火山，看上去就像这世界在一场惩罚性的大火之后可能变成的样子。

text_en: Climbing past Humboldt's footprints toward the snowcap of Chimborazo, the narrator is seized by a kind of delirium at the summit, where an old man appears to him, introduces himself as Time, and tells him to go back down and tell people what he has seen.
text_zh: 叙述者踩着洪堡的足迹向钦博拉索山的雪顶攀登，到了山顶，他陷入一种狂热的谵妄；一位老人出现在他面前，自称“时间”，吩咐他下山去，把在这里看到的告诉世人。
